content.text:
I've submitted index 28 (Fe 0.53, Ni 0.18, V 0.29) as the best composition. It measured 1.8e-7 A, but that result is thin: I used all 3 photocurrent measurements on 3 of the 160 compositions.

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.53 / 0.18 / 0.29 | 1.8e-7 |
| 119 | 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.20 | 1.8e-7 |
| 123 | 0.22 / 0.18 / 0.60 | 4e-8 |

- **Fe-rich beats V-rich:** the two Fe-rich, low-Ni films gave about 4.5 times the photocurrent of the V-rich film. I picked them because of the general tendency for iron–vanadium oxides to be the light-active part at this photon energy (2.4 eV).
- **The tie:** 28 and 119 gave the same photocurrent. I chose 28 because it has less Ni, which on the same general tendency I'd expect to be a slight advantage. The data themselves don't separate the two.
- **Not tested:** I measured nothing in the Ni-rich region (Ni above 0.5) or in between the three points. I left it out because Ni-rich oxides are usually poor at this, not because of any measurement here.
- **Unused tools:** I used none of the 5 XRD scans and didn't look at the known-phase list (it was too long to load). So which crystal phases are present is a guess, not something I checked.
